result.summary: This is a typical residential mid-block environment with a continuous sidewalk and on-street parallel parking. While the street is relatively narrow, which may naturally slow traffic, the pedestrian environment lacks a buffer from the roadway and suffers from visual obstructions due to parked vehicles and dense vegetation.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and dense, overhanging vegetation significantly limit sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the street where cars are parked and trees/bushes overhang the walkway.

hazards.name: Narrow Effective Walkway
hazards.description: The sidewalk is narrow and its usable width is further reduced by encroaching vegetation.
hazards.location_in_image: The sidewalk area behind the parked brown SUV.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim overhanging trees and bushes to ensure the full width of the sidewalk is clear and to improve visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the driveway and potential crossing points to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: If space permits, introduce a planting strip or furniture zone between the sidewalk and the curb to increase pedestrian comfort and safety.
